author: NorthEast News Desk
body: DFO Management, the investment vehicle backed by Dell Technologies founder and CEO Michael Dell, and Sequence Holdings have agreed to take Baldwin Group private in a transaction valued at $7.7 billion, Reuters reported Monday.

Baldwin shareholders are expected to receive $32.50 in cash per share. Reuters said the offer represented an 88% premium to the company’s unaffected share price before reports of a possible deal began circulating.

Baldwin provides insurance brokerage, risk-management and technology-enabled underwriting services. The buyers said private ownership would give the company more flexibility to make long-term investments, including in artificial-intelligence capabilities, without the same pressure as a public quarterly reporting cycle.

The transaction is expected to close during the first quarter of 2027, subject to the required approvals and closing conditions. Eligible employees will have an opportunity to retain a minority stake by rolling over part of their holdings, according to the report.

The deal is another example of investors using private capital to fund technology upgrades in established service businesses. It also places a large insurance brokerage transaction among the day’s notable mergers and acquisitions.
dek: DFO Management and Sequence Holdings will acquire insurance broker Baldwin Group in a deal designed to give the company more flexibility for AI investment.
headline: Michael Dell-backed group agrees to take Baldwin private for $7.7 billion
